title: Horse race of weekly idiosyncratic momentum strategies with respect to various risk metrics: Evidence from the Chinese stock market

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper evaluates weekly momentum (MOM) and idiosyncratic momentum (IMOM) strategies in the Chinese A-share market. Idiosyncratic returns are estimated using Fama-French 5-factor regressions on daily excess returns over past J weeks. Portfolios are formed by sorting stocks into deciles based on cumulative raw or idiosyncratic returns (with a 1-week skip to avoid microstructure effects) and held for K weeks. Additionally, risk-adjusted IMOM strategies are constructed by directly dividing idiosyncratic returns by various idiosyncratic risk metrics (such as idiosyncratic volatility, skewness, kurtosis, maximum drawdown, expected shortfall, and VaR) or indirectly via bivariate double sorting.
extraction.universe: Chinese A-share common stocks listed on Shanghai Stock Exchange (SHSE) and Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE)

key_findings: A prevailing contrarian effect (short-term reversal) exists for raw returns, while a pronounced idiosyncratic momentum (IMOM) effect is observed when sorting on idiosyncratic returns.
Most idiosyncratic risk metrics (especially idiosyncratic volatility and idiosyncratic maximum drawdown) exhibit a negative relation with cross-sectional stock returns.

Bivariate double-sorted portfolios (indirect adjustment) of IMOM with idiosyncratic risk metrics (like ISkew, IMD, IES, and IVaR) significantly enhance profitability compared to univariate risk-sorted portfolios.
IVol-based and IMD-based IMOM portfolios show superior performance and have strong explanatory power over other risk-adjusted IMOM portfolios in spanning tests.

The profitability of IMOM and risk-adjusted IMOM strategies is highly dependent on market conditions, performing significantly better during upside market states, high market liquidity, and high investor sentiment.
limitations: Costly short-selling in the Chinese stock market, which limits arbitrage efficiency.
Price limit trading rules (±10% daily fluctuation limit) that slow down or speed up price adjustments to news.
Retail investors in China are highly under-diversified, holding an average of only 1.4 stocks as of June 2018.
Potential microstructure biases (bid-ask spread, non-synchronous trading, lack of liquidity) require skipping a week between the estimation and holding periods.
